newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-TAYLOR TO STEP DOWN FROM TEST TEAM-PAPER.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAYLOR TO STEP DOWN FROM TEST TEAM-PAPER.

text.p: Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor has told close friends he will step down from the test team after a run of low scores and a recent torrent of criticism, Sydney's Daily Telegraph newspaper reported on Monday.

"Captain Mark Taylor has decided to step down from the Australian cricket team for the first Ashes test, finally conceding defeat after 18 months of disastrous form," the tabloid newspaper said in a front page report.
"Taylor has told only a close circle of friends about his decision," the Telegraph said.
The report was written after Taylor scored five in the first innings of a three day match against Derbyshire, but before his overnight 59 not out in the second innings of that match.
The second innings half century was only Taylor's third first class 50 in 18 months and he has not scored a test half century since late 1995.
Criticism of Taylor and the Australian selectors has reached a crescendo in recent days, with former Australian test captains Ian Chappell and Greg Chappell calling for his dismissal.
Ian Chappell said selectors lacked the courage to sack Taylor while Greg Chappell suggested he was not in a mentally fit state to lead Australia on the current tour of England.
The Telegraph said Taylor, who is one of a panel of three Australian selectors on tour, had decided to bow out in favour of vice-captain Steve Waugh, who is also on the selection panel.
